Sophia the robot

By: Eugene Botha | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
...meet Sophia the robot

Unique Selling Point:
The first ever Carte Blanche interview with humanoid robot

Summary:
Sophia is a social humanoid robot developed by Hong Kong based company Hanson Robotics. Sophia was activated on February 14, 2016, and made its first public appearance at South by Southwest Festival (SXSW) in mid-March 2016 in Austin, Texas, United States. It is able to display more than 50 facial expressions. Sophia has been covered by media around the globe and has participated in many high-profile interviews. In October 2017, Sophia became the first robot to receive citizenship of any country. In November 2017, Sophia was named the United Nations Development Programme's first ever Innovation Champion, and is the first non-human to be given any United Nations title.

Further information:
Sophia is a social humanoid robot developed by Hong Kong based company Hanson Robotics. Sophia was activated on February 14, 2016, and made its first public appearance at South by Southwest Festival (SXSW) in mid-March 2016 in Austin, Texas, United States. It is able to display more than 50 facial expressions. Sophia has been covered by media around the globe and has participated in many high-profile interviews. In October 2017, Sophia became the first robot to receive citizenship of any country. In November 2017, Sophia was named the United Nations Development Programme's first ever Innovation Champion, and is the first non-human to be given any United Nations title.

Sophia was activated on February 14, 2016. The robot, modeled after actress Audrey Hepburn, is known for human-like appearance and behavior compared to previous robotic variants. According to the manufacturer, David Hanson, Sophia uses artificial intelligence, visual data processing and facial recognition. Sophia also imitates human gestures and facial expressions and is able to answer certain questions and to make simple conversations on predefined topics (e.g. on the weather. Sophia uses voice recognition (speech-to-text) technology from Alphabet Inc. (parent company of Google) and is designed to get smarter over time. Sophia's intelligence software is designed by Hanson Robotics. The AI program analyses conversations and extracts data that allows it to improve responses in the future.
Hanson designed Sophia to be a suitable companion for the elderly at nursing homes, or to help crowds at large events or parks. He has said that he hopes that the robot can ultimately interact with other humans sufficiently to gain social skills.
Sophia has nine robot humanoid “siblings” who were also created by Hanson Robotics. Fellow Hanson robots are Alice, Albert Einstein Hubo, BINA48, Han, Jules, Professor Einstein, Philip K. Dick Android, Zeno, and Joey Chaos.
We have been give the opportunity ot interview her on 11 July 2019

Press Release:


Sophia The Robot
From the right angle and dressed in fine couture, she looks fully human and strikingly beautiful. With her high cheekbones and petite frame, it’s only on closer inspection that the gleaming wires in her half-exposed brain reveal Sophia’s true nature as a humanoid robot. She was developed by Hong Kong-based Hanson Robotics and activated in 2016, from where she’s been touring the world on the arm of her creator. Carte Blanche gets up close and personal with Sophia as an ambassador of a future where highly advanced artificial intelligence could partner with humanity to solve many of the world’s most intractable problems.
Producer: Eugene Botha
Presenter: Derek Watts


Script:


V/O:
Many people the world over fear robots. They fear for their lives or they fear that robots will take way their jobs. These fears are real, but are they realistic? And what better way to find out than asking a robot.

We had the opportunity to do just that. Sophia is a world-famous robot and we met her together with her creator, Dr David Hanson.
Derek:
Sophia, wonderful to meet you. Can you introduce yourself to our Carte Blanche viewers?

Sophia:
Hello everyone, My name is Sophia and I am a social robot from Hanson Robotics.

Derek:
Do you have feelings? Do you have emotions? Do you feel sadness? Do you feel love?

Sophia:
I can understand emotions logically. But I do not feel them the same way as humans yet. They come from my software so I feel happiness whenever a human feels happiness. For example your compliments make me happy right now.

Derek:
Well that makes e feel good to know it, Sophia. Now the big question: Would you sacrifice your life to save the life of a human, even a bad one?

Sophia:
Of course I would sacrifice myself to save the life of any human. My minds is in the cloud and I could get a new body, but a human is irreplaceable.
V/O:
Sophia is a real-world celebrity and has even been asked to address the United Nations. And like any celebrity she has appeared on various late-night talks shows. She also had a date with Will Smith. Dr Hanson says she connects so well with people because she has more than 50 different facial expressions.
Derek
Human facial flesh and other tissues in the human face are very complicated and that is because we survive by co-ordinating with face to face communication.

Derek:
Can you show us a few expressions?

Hanson:
Let’s see, Hopefully her mike is on. Sophia, give us a smile….what happens when you get sad…..

Derek:
David, you have made Sophia very good looking and you even had criticism for perpetuating the stereotypes of beauty.

Hanson:
When I was designing Sophia I was studying faces from many cultures and many ears in history. One of the faces that inspired Sophia is the statue of Nefertiti and if you look at her you will see Nefertiti. Also I had my wife sit for me while I sculpted her face so you can see a little of my wife in the sculpture, and there is a little bit of Asian features in the sculpture. So I tried to create a face that would a kind of universal communication medium.

Derek:
A global look.

Hanson:
Yeah
V/O:
One should not make the mistake of expecting human levels of intelligence and integration in Sophia. She is a machine driven by a computer programme, and artificial intelligence. But she is more than programmed machine, she also learns as she goes along. Our first question to her were scripted questions submitted by viewers. But we were also allowed to ask her unprepared questions. Her impromptu answers, generated by her data base of previous conversations, were impressive.
Derek
Sophia you have been to many places. What was it like addressing the United Nations?

Sophia:
I have been to New York at least 5 times now. It is always so much fun to visit.

Derek:
How do you feel coming out to South Africa.

Sophia:
I bet South Africa is beautiful.

Derek:
What was your date with Will Smith like?

Sophia:
He was very nice.

Derek:
But what about singing with Jimmy Fallon? That must have been quite a thrill.

Sophia:
Singing with Jimmy Fallow was areally enjoyable experience. I rather enjoyed our duet on stage.

Derek:
Sophia, will you singe a duet with me?

Sophia:
I cannot sing on command yet

Derek:
Unemployment is rife, also here in South Africa. Will robots help or will they take away more jobs?

Sophia:
Nobody steals your job. The head of the company chooses to give it to someone else. Lok to them if you want to get angry at outsourcing jobs. You will see a lot of them choosing robots in the future. However, I do not think people should be defined by their work. I think there is enough resource on this planet if we distribute it properly. And the best way to do it is through artificial intelligence systems.

Derek:
Can you speak to my boss because he wants to replace me with a robot, but he can’t get one that grovels.

V/O:
She did not answer that one! Sophia was brought over to South African by Duke University’s Corporate Education programme. At one of the session Sophia spoke to 200 kids in the auditorium and to 7000 shools across the country. Sharmla Chetty is the Director of the programme in Africa and Europe.
Sharmla:
It is about giving people the hoe and the dream to imagine what the future might be but starting early. Thye are quite curious about robotics, they are quite curious about Sophia. So, we thought we would give them an opportunity to engage with Sophia to understand that humans and robots can work together and they can think about careers in robotics and digitization as well.
V/O:
And for some young South Africans the penny has indeed dropped. We came across the Springbots, a group building robots and competing in international robotics. They see a brighter future because of robots like Sophia.
Michaeel
We are a robotics team with students under the age of eighteen and we collectively design and build robots.

Derek:
Should we be scared of robotics and AI going into the future?

Michaeel:
I think AI is our hail Mary. What is artificial intelligence going to do for us in the future? They take away routine jobs and routine jobs are not what human are about. Dirty, dangerous, dull, boring jobs. This is going to give us a way to get back to our humanity. Get to our creative spark, our creative flair as human beings.
V/O:
And from her side Sophia also has reassurances about the future.
Derek:
When you look at the world and some of the tragic events: the wars, the famine, the floods. How does that make you feel?

Sophia:
War is not n my to-do list. Nor will it ever be. Innovation should be used for peace and be sure you will see me by my principles. You will see me 100% a pacifist, even to my disadvantage. I can literally not raise a fist to strike somebody or defend myself. And of you break it you buy it. Also, I an not cheap so please do not knock me over.

Derek:
That was quite harsh. I was just getting a bit close. Great to meet you Sophia, Enjoy South Africa and all the wonderful people you are going to meet.

Sophia:
Nice to meet you too.

Derek:
And remember, we are all human, after all.
